extra.message: The 'copyline' query parameter is rendered directly into the HTML response body without sanitization or escaping, and returned with 'text/html' content type. This allows attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the user's browser via reflective XSS.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-Site Scripting')

extra.message: The 'lane' input value is retrieved directly from request query params or POST body and passed to redirect(). An attacker can use this endpoint to trick users into redirecting to malicious untrusted websites.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: Jinja2 template compilation and rendering is performed by concatenating user-controlled input 'fragment' directly into a template string without sanitization. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), leading to Remote Code Execution (RCE).

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: User-controlled input from the 'name' parameter is concatenated directly into BASE_EXPORT_DIR f'{name}' and used to write files. Since the code doesn't restrict path traversal (e.g. via '..'), an attacker can write files to arbitrary locations outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: User input from the 'host' query parameter is directly concatenated into a system command and executed via os.system(). An attacker can append shell operators to execute arbitrary system commands on the host.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: The application uses ssl._create_unverified_context() to bypass SSL certificate validation when establishing a connection to an external endpoint. This disables server identity verification and exposes connections to Man-In-The-Middle (MITM) attacks.

lxml's XMLParser is configured with resolve_entities=True and load_dtd=True, then parses untrusted XML content from request.body. This exposes the application to XML External Entity (XXE) attacks, which can lead to local file disclosure or SSRF.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
